svg.aria-label: Diagram: three AWS Backup controls and the way each one can fail without producing an error. The lifecycle control is silent on unsupported resource types, because the Lifecycle API reference states that AWS Backup ignores this expression for other resource types, so a cold storage tiering setting is accepted, displayed and never applied. Tag-based resource assignment is silent because service opt-in still applies when only tags are used, so a correctly tagged resource in a service that has not been opted into is not backed up and the backup plan shows no error; opt-in is set per account and per Region. The vault lock is not silent about new jobs, since new backup and copy jobs that do not conform to the lock's retention window fail, but it is silent about recovery points already in the vault, which keep their previous lifecycle settings. The diagram also records the arithmetic the lifecycle forces: backups transitioned to cold storage must be stored there for a minimum of 90 days, so the retention setting must be 90 days greater than the transition setting, meaning a transition at 30 days forces a retention floor of 120 days. Finally it lists three documented boundaries on compliance mode immutability: closing the account suspends it for 90 days and then AWS deletes the vault contents even if vault lock was in place, the lock does not govern the Amazon EC2 APIs ModifySnapshotAttribute and ModifySnapshotTier, and a disabled AMI can block restore of EC2 recovery points even under a vault lock or legal hold.
svg.title: Three controls, three silences, and the boundaries on the word immutable
svg.text: A setting that is ignored looks exactly like a setting that is working.
AWS Backup — three controls, and what each one does when you get it wrong.
LIFECYCLE — silent on resource types that cannot tier
“Resource types that can transition to cold storage are listed in the Feature availability by resource table.
AWS Backup ignores this expression for other resource types.”
Not rejected, not warned. The plan saves, the setting renders, nothing tiers.
RESOURCE ASSIGNMENT — silent on the gate that is not in the plan
“If you only use tags for resource assignment, then the service opt-in settings will still apply.”
Right tag, right plan, zero coverage. Opt-in lives under Settings — per account, per Region.
So one plan deployed to two Regions can protect different things.
VAULT LOCK — loud about new jobs, silent about what is already there
LOUD: “New backup and copy jobs created in the vault will fail if they do not conform to the retention
periods you set” — a failed job is feedback.
SILENT: “Recovery points that were present in the vault prior to the vault lock being enabled will follow
their previous lifecycle settings.” A seven-year minimum extends nothing already in the vault.
The arithmetic tiering forces on you
“must be stored in cold storage for a minimum of 90 days”
transition 30 + cold minimum 90 = delete 120
Cold storage buys a lower rate by removing your ability
to delete early. It raises the retention floor.
Two clocks, and only one is running out
Protection starts at Locked: true — it blocks deletes
“regardless of whether you are still in the cooling-off
grace time period”.
LockDate is your deadline to change your mind, not the
date the data becomes protected.
“Immutable … by any user or by AWS” has three documented boundaries
1. Close the account and after 90 days “AWS deletes the contents of your backup vault, even if AWS Backup
Vault Lock was in place” — immutability belongs to the vault, not to the account that owns it.
2. It governs AWS Backup, not EC2: ModifySnapshotAttribute still shares, ModifySnapshotTier still retiers.
3. A disabled AMI blocks restore of EC2 recovery points — intact, undeletable, and not restorable.
The audit: ask the plan three questions it will not answer.
Which resource types can tier? Which services are opted in, per Region? And has LockDate passed?
